title: Telescoping Lantern Mast with Ground Spike (3 sections, twist-lock)
description: Three nested tubes with a ground spike and a hang-eye. Each joint is a bayonet L-slot with a pinch detent, so it extends from a 142 mm packed stick to roughly 0.3 m and locks without tools.
use: Camp-site lantern / bunting / bird-call-speaker pole for tents and picnics: push the spike into soft ground, twist-lock to height, hang a lightweight lantern or flag from the eye.
material: PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 4 perimeters, 20% infill. Lantern load: designed for about 0.3 kg (untested). Print tubes upright; spike section is printed point-up.

problem_solved: Few lantern/flag poles pack small AND need no tools: this one replaces fiddly tent-pole bits with 3 printed tubes that twist-lock, with the ground spike built in.
mechanism: Bayonet L-slot per joint (2 pegs 180 deg apart): 3.0 mm pegs ride 3.6 mm vertical slots, then a 35 deg arc arm; the last 6.5 deg of the arm is 3.2 mm tall = light pinch detent. Gravity seats the pegs on the slot floor.
tolerances: Radial nesting clearance 0.5 mm; peg-in-slot 0.3 mm each side (vertical), 0.1 mm at the detent; pegs end 0.5 mm below the outer surface so they never snag.
assembly: 1. Print the three tubes (tube 1 prints spike-up).
2. Drop tube 2 into tube 1 (pegs line up with the open slots), then tube 3 into tube 2.
3. To extend: pull tube 2 up along the slot until it stops, twist ~35 deg to lock; repeat for tube 3.
fit_notes: Peg tips and slots are small; keep tubes clean of grit. Spike is blunt-tipped (1.2 mm radius) for ground use only - not a weapon.
